additional_info.body:
Hello everyone,
We are currently conducting tests with the eActros 600 on the Transports DUBOC charging station (ref. SiD MP / R6 170002075) and are encountering an issue: the charging sessions are cutting off, as shown in the attached photos.
The problem appears to come mainly from the left connector (CCS2 rated at 240 kW), where we are observing repeated interruptions.
We are also testing the right connector, currently limited to 80 kW, which seems to be working fine. With Franck’s support, we plan to unlock it up to 150 kW to expand the testing range.
It’s important to alert the teams — François Catalina, Antoine Breillat, and Emmanuel Neveu — since this situation seems similar to an issue previously observed on other sites.
The goal is to determine whether this is a hardware or software fault on the charger, or if external disturbances are causing the charging to stop at certain power levels.
We will continue running tests at different power levels throughout the day to collect as much data as possible.
Best regards,

additional_info.subject: Ticket Request – Malfunctions Observed During eActros 600 / Volvo FH Electric Tests (SiD MP / R6 170002075)
additional_info.body:
Hello,
On the Sicharge D – SiD MP / R6 170002075 charging station, we carried out several tests with Olivier — he was on site, and I was connected remotely:
• CCS2-2 connector: eActros 600 connected
• CCS1-1 connector: Volvo FH Electric connected
Observation 1 (10:30 AM)
It was impossible to disconnect the eActros 600, even after remotely stopping the charging session.
A full restart of the charger was required to release the connector.
Observation 2 (11:00 AM)
After disconnecting both the Volvo FH (100% charged) and the Mercedes, then reconnecting the Volvo, the physical communication was properly established (green light on the truck side, blue on the Sicharge D side).
However, the steps displayed on the screen did not fully validate, preventing any further action on connector 2.
This issue occurred multiple times, blocking the CCS2 connector and preventing charging of the eActros 600.
Observation 3 (11:30 AM)
We encountered a complete lock-up: it was impossible to unplug the eActros 600 due to repeated charging session initialization failures.
Olivier suspects a hardware or internal control issue, as the charger remains stuck in a “connecting” state, even when attempting to start a session with the Mercedes.
Observation 4 (11:38 AM)
After several additional attempts, when connecting the eActros 600, only the first parameter “Connection” is validated on the screen, while the subsequent steps do not proceed.
However, the eActros 600 appearing as “connected” on the screen seems to be a result of a connection failure with the Volvo FH on the right-side connector (CCS No.1).
Observation 5 (11:38 AM)
It took about one hour to establish a stable connection with the Volvo on the CCS1 connector, which finally allowed us to operate on the CCS2 connector and continue the tests.
Observation 6 (11:55 AM)
The connection with the eActros 600 eventually worked, although we still don’t understand exactly why it succeeded this time.
Fortunately, we managed to restore functionality, ensuring that operations on Monday can proceed normally.
However, the client is asking: Why didn’t it work at first? And why did both truck brands experience connection difficulties?
Please open an investigation ticket to analyze these anomalies and determine the root cause of the connector lock and session failures.
Best regards,
